# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

### Nov 2, 2026
1 5:37p ○ Scheduler.run_all sleeps after every job, including the last
2 " ● Scheduler.run_all now sleeps only between jobs
3 5:41p ○ Schedule library does not catch job exceptions; docs prescribe a catch_exceptions decorator
S1 Pick up the failing-jobs change in run_pending for the schedule library. Current progress: investigation only, no implementation yet. (Nov 2, 5:41 PM)
**Investigated**: The working tree diff, which contains only the run_all change (sleep skipped after the last job). The run_pending and run_all definitions in schedule/__init__.py. Branch and stash state: fix/job-errors exists alongside main and master, with no commits ahead of main and no stashes. Exception-handling docs in docs/exception-handling.rst, docs/faq.rst, and docs/index.rst.

**Learned**: run_pending (schedule/__init__.py ~line 89) runs sorted runnable jobs with no error handling, so an exception from one job stops the loop. The library documents this as intended behavior and recommends a user-side catch_exceptions decorator. The memory store has no saved work state for this project.

**Completed**: No changes to run_pending have been made. The only uncommitted change is the earlier run_all fix, which stops sleeping after the final job.

**Next Steps**: Waiting for the user to specify which failing-jobs behavior is wanted. Candidates: continue past failures and log them, add an opt-in setting so default behavior is unchanged, or ensure failed jobs still have next_run updated. Also pending: whether the run_all change is committed before or separately from the new work.

**Notes**: The requested change is ambiguous, and the session has asked the user to choose an option before proceeding. The fix/job-errors branch has no commits yet, so the failing-jobs work would be the first commit on that branch.
